```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A has a business payer with documented willingness to pay. Competitor pricing is sourced across Canny, Frill, Featul and Userback, and a 62-tool pricing study puts the median entry plan at $29-$31.50/mo with top tiers around $270/mo. Idea B's only price anchor is one consumer product at $5/mo.",
    "At $25-$79/mo per customer, A needs only a handful of buyers to show traction within 90 days. B's $5/mo consumer price needs far more customers to matter.",
    "B's brief raises a direct legal risk to its core mechanic: scraping and AI-rewriting third-party news sits inside active publisher copyright litigation. A's compliance needs (a data processing agreement, a privacy policy and GDPR/CCPA records) are routine, one-time setup items.",
    "B's stronger, higher-value payer hypothesis (local publishers licensing the tool) has no supporting evidence, and its publisher partnership channel is marked [unsourced]. Both count as missing.",
    "B's brief says only ~9% of Americans pay for local news, which works against a consumer payer base. B also lacks reliable local data feeds, which makes the 'local' differentiator hard to deliver.",
    "Both ideas are crowded. A's brief at least sketches buildable wedges (AI-native triage, a vertical, a pricing break) that fit one operator with AI agents. A's demand quotes include a buyer complaining about $50-80/mo pricing, which points to room for a cheaper entrant."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence is three reader letters (2008, 2017, ~2022) complaining about bloated print newspapers. None shows willingness to pay for a customized product, and the Concord Monitor letter argues the paper is not worth $130 at all. That supports price resistance more than demand. The publisher-side payer and channel have no evidence at all.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A is clearly better on payer quality, pricing evidence and legal risk. But A's brief admits heavy saturation (73 tools, standard free tiers, rising Google Ads CPC) and gives no achievable customer acquisition cost. A's 90-day first-customer path depends on finding a niche wedge the brief does not show is open."
}
```
